questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good opportunities for receiving a spot, very international atmosphere, lots of other Danes, interesting culture and food.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult, confusing and frustrating

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Only a little bit of assistance from the international office in Milano, and apart from that a lot of assistance from fellow Danish exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to have some connections with former exchange students in Milano that had rented an apartment privately. However it seemed quite easy for most Danes to find housing through different webpages.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus is basically the only option, but it is highly recommended as it allows you to indulge in the local culture and life.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Terrible experience, very stressful and frustrating, but it all ended up well; Italians are very laissez-faire.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Extremely bureaucratic and confusing; you don't really know what you are supposed to do, and the International Office seems just as confused about the registration process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Just the "help" from the International Office. Without the help from former Danish exchange students, I would not have made it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy and very open. You could simply attend any lectures for a certain period before actually signing up for the course, meaning that you can test different options and see what fits you best.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be chill about, it all works out in the end, and basically anything is possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Although I was a BA student and attended only MA courses, the academical level was generally lower than what I was used to. Most professors are extremely chill and easy to work with, and it is almost impossible not to pass all courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was in fact quite similar. The only difference was that it was a lot less structured and less demanding than what I am used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Biopolitics and Intellectuals, popular culture and collective identies are both very interesting. The other two were not really, but they were easy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spent a lot of money on experiences like food, trips, nights out, souvenirs and so on. It makes the stay much better to take part in all these activities with your fellow exchange students (I only did it with other Danes).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, eating at restaurants, and transportation was much cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not take part in any activities organised by the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I do not know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of other Danes, and I really recommend taking part in the Danish community. Also taking time to get to know some locals and visiting other places in Italy has given me a lot.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Day trips to other parts of Italy, walking around new neighborhoods, having friends from home over.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as the Italian culture is surprisingly similar to that of Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Only place I did it was in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Italians are much less efficient and everything goes very slowly. The Italians simply do not care as much about it as Danes, and although it was exhausting in the beginning, it was very inspiring.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food culture, social culture, drinking culture, culture culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Save up a lot of money, because you do not want to have to miss out on experiences because of a lack of money. 
Learn a bit of Italian before going, the locals actually appreciate it and just the basics can do a whole lot. 
Everything works out in the end, so do not stress too much about all of the details, like I did.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Academics come second, all the things that happen outside of university are what makes the exchange worth it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a lot of new people, living in a different culture, feeling like a local, the feeling of being on holidays for half a year.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All of the bureaucratic things before going abroad. Also being away from friends and family for so long.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
